lever: redfirst (built by the fastapi agent, reused): one sentence group at the end of step 2: before the first edit, run the issue's example as a python3 heredoc that asserts the result the issue asks for and, for one ordinary input, the result the code gives today; the first assert must fail now (if it passes, the example misses the bug, so change it); rerun the same check after each edit until both asserts pass.
tokens_added: 72 Gemma tokens (fastapi agent's count; v13's prompt is 840)
why: Mechanism: no run ever saw the bug. Every check any of the six runs wrote used a pure-CJK string (わさび, こんにちは, 你好你好, 这是一个测试), and at the base commit all 21 pure-CJK inputs at widths 2-8 wrap correctly, while 39 of 63 inputs with a 1-3 character ASCII prefix lose or reorder a character (measured, scripts/forty_two/rich_solve/ev_redfirst_3180.py): the fold must fall inside a double-width character, as the issue says. p4_b1024 (v13's line) ran three green probes (118-268 s) and spent thinking turns of 36-78 s explaining why the code looked right, never edited, and hit the cap; p4_v0t2 wrote one green repro at 155 s, then a 147 s turn; p4_v7 ran 7 green chop_cells probes and 4 green repro rewrites. Under the rule a green first check means 'change the example', and the nearest change toward the issue's wording is red in most cases; its output shows a missing character and points at chop_cells' reversed chunks, whose one-token fix passes all 114 target tests (write-up). The rule's rerun-after-each-edit with an ordinary-input assert also covers p4_v7d, which had the fix but broke 7 existing wrap tests and ran nothing. Evidence: docs/forty_two/evidence/rich_solve_redfirst.txt. Applies outside the 42: rich_3043 and fastapi_11194 were solved on p4_b1024 with no check before the first edit (the fastapi agent's census), and any hidden task whose first probe happens to miss the bug.
alternative: submissions/v13_modtests (commit 520358f5) for the p4_v7d failure mode only (4 existing failures in tests/test_text.py visible in 0.3 s); it does nothing for the current line, which never edited.
expected: maybe: the lever makes the bug visible; finding chop_cells' reversal and making the small fix still has to happen inside the time left (1 of 12 L4 runs solved it, at 140 s)
baseline: p4 (v5h2), p4_v7, p4_v7c, p4_v7d, p4_b1024 (v12-b1024), p4_v0t2 (v0-think) all failed; 1 of 12 Kaggle L4 runs solved (g4-l4-v4)
regression_risk: As the fastapi agent measured for this bundle: an extra check call (10-17 s of model time on the box) before the first edit on every task; most exposed are tasks solved at the cap through the fallback diff (rich_3506, rich_3521, fastapi_14458 on p4_b1024), and tasks with no runnable example, where the 'change it' clause can cost a second call. Rich-specific: when the symptom depends on input shape (as here), the model may try several green inputs before a red one; the sentence sets no limit. Inferred.
box_risk: Text-call leaks are not new (10 leaked replies over the six earlier box runs, all recovered after the nudge); new on the v13 screen is one first-reply leak that never recovered (fastapi_14487), cause undecided, v13 not treated as broken. The bundle inherits v13's fenced heredoc in step 3; its added sentences have no code fence, backtick or tool-call syntax (tests/test_v13_fastapi_levers.py). A sample with 0 tool calls points at the base, not at this lever.
tests: tests/test_v13_fastapi_levers.py (the fastapi agent's: v13 plus exactly that sentence, no fence or call syntax, <= 90 tokens, no leakage, validate.py)
